items.paragraph: Work with the body. Sometimes the mind is too activated for meditation to help, so you may need to work directly with the body to calm it down. Maybe get a massage, or massage a foot, your scalp, a temple, or the back of the neck, the top of a shoulder, etc. (Avoid massaging the front of the neck. Choice: you can answer the question, write an answer, write that you don't know, take a break, rephrase the question, ask someone else, stop doing this, etc. Autonomous signal: write whatever you get (a word, sensation, impulse, objection, or silence) without interpreting it as proof. Deepener: none (full alertness isn't a lesser version). Handoff: have your adult self answer the question in whatever way is appropriate, preferably by writing or doing. Integration/exit: reality test the signal and do one small thing based on it. Since you didn't go into trance, just close the exercise and carry on with your day.

published: The induction and inner meeting bring you to a place where you can listen. From here, learn to answer what happens instead of reciting a speech that has already decided what every part will say. Read these examples before practicing, then put the screen aside.

Observable pacing: Keep the eyes open, name the room and day, feel the feet, and read or write in ordinary awareness. Invitation: Ask one clear question and wait without narrowing attention further. Genuine choice: Answer, write “unsure,” rest, change the question, seek another person’s view, or stop. Autonomous signal: Record a word, sensation, impulse, objection, or silence without interpreting it as proof. Deepener: None. Full alertness is not an inferior version of the practice. Handoff: Let the internal adult respond in writing or through one practical choice. Integration and exit: Reality-test the signal and do one small action. Because no altered state was cultivated, simply close the exercise and continue the day.
